findings.title: Dataclass field default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time, not per-instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain field default, which in Python is evaluated exactly once, when the class body is executed at module import. Every `AssignmentSource` created afterwards without explicitly passing `queued` (including every call to `AssignmentSource.from_integration(...)`, which is the only constructor used throughout the PR) will get the exact same frozen timestamp -- the time the module was first imported (e.g. process/worker startup) -- rather than the actual time the assignment source was created. This silently produces incorrect/misleading `queued` values for the lifetime of the process. It should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead of a bare default expression.

findings.title: test_to_dict does not catch the stale/shared default timestamp bug
findings.body: `test_to_dict` only asserts `result.get("queued") is not None`, which passes trivially even with the eager-default-evaluation bug in `AssignmentSource.queued` (see finding in assignment_source.py). No test verifies that two different `AssignmentSource` instances created at different times actually get different `queued` values, so the bug goes undetected.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` parameter added to abstract sync_status_outbound is never populated by any caller
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature was extended with `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, mirroring the loop-prevention mechanism added for assignee sync. However, nothing in this PR (or shown in the diff) ever passes a non-None value for this parameter from any inbound status-sync code path, nor does `should_sync` for the `outbound_status` attribute get checked against it anywhere. As written, this is dead/unused scaffolding: the status-sync cycle (resolve/unresolve flapping analogous to the assignee flapping this PR fixes) is not actually addressed, despite the interface now suggesting support for it. This risks misleading future maintainers into thinking status-sync loops are already handled.

findings.title: Loop-prevention check is scoped to integration, not to the specific external issue that triggered the change
findings.body: `should_sync` suppresses outbound sync whenever `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`, matching only on integration id. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` iterates over every `GroupLink`/`ExternalIssue` tied to the group and invokes `sync_assignee_outbound` for each one. If a single Group happens to be linked to more than one `ExternalIssue` under the same integration (e.g. multiple linked issues within the same Jira/GitHub instance), an inbound change originating from one of those external issues will also suppress the outbound sync to the other, unrelated external issue tracked by the same integration, even though that other issue was not the source of the loop and should still receive the update.
